chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is nothing which obliterates Islam as much as greed obliterates it.' Then he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'For this greed has a creeping nature like the creeping of an ant, and branches like the branches of polytheism.' And in another copy, 'thorns'.

key_terms.الدَّبِيبُ: Creeping or crawling slowly, implying a gradual, insidious process
key_terms.الشَّوْكِ: Thorns, an alternative description for the branches of greed
key_terms.الشُّحِّ: Greed or stinginess, specifically the devouring of wealth and faith
key_terms.الشِّرَكِ: Polytheism or associating partners with God, used here as a metaphor for the branching nature of greed
key_terms.مَحَقَ: To obliterate, destroy, or wipe out completely

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet say about the destructive nature of greed in Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) identified greed (al-shuhh) as the most destructive force to Islam, surpassing all other vices. He metaphorically describes its insidious nature as creeping slowly like an ant and branching out like polytheism (or thorns), highlighting how it subtly corrupts faith and leads to spiritual ruin. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on purifying the heart from greed as a prerequisite for maintaining the integrity of Islamic belief and practice.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa, 
(It has been narrated) from Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘There is nothing which obliterates (destroys) Al-Islam (more) than its destruction by the greedy one’. Then he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘For this greed is a crawl like the crawling of an ant, and a branch like the branch of Polytheism’. And in another copy, ‘Thorn’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Sadaqah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, has narrated from his father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘No other thing is more effacing to Islam than stinginess.’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘Greediness creeps like an ant and has branches (or thorns) like polytheism.’”
